items.en: What did Julius hear?
items.hint: an accusative with infinitive (that the dog ...)

items.en: Where did the letter-carrier arrive from?
items.hint: a town name in the ablative (place from which, no preposition)

items.en: Does the doorkeeper know who sent the letter?
items.hint: a yes/no answer (he does not know)

items.en: By whom was the letter sent?
items.hint: ablative after 'ā' (by whom)

items.q: Cūr Iūlius hās litterās legere nōn vult?
items.en: Why doesn't Julius want to read this letter?
items.hint: a reason: the master is demanding ... (accusative)

items.q: Quot mēnsium mercēdem Iūlius magistrō dēbet?
items.en: How many months' fee does Julius owe the master?
items.hint: a number in the genitive (of ... months)

items.en: What does Julius break?
items.hint: a noun in the accusative (the object)

items.q: Quālis discipulus est Mārcus, ut magister scrībit?
items.en: What kind of pupil is Marcus, as the master writes?
items.hint: two adjectives in the nominative

items.q: Cūr magister Mārcum nihil docēre potest?
items.en: Why can the master teach Marcus nothing?
items.hint: a reason clause with 'quia' (he himself wants ...)

items.en: Is the fee handed over to the master on time?
items.hint: a yes/no answer (never)

items.en: In what state does Marcus watch his father reading?
items.hint: an adjective in the nominative (agreeing with Marcus)

items.en: Why is the boy pale?
items.hint: accusative after 'ob' (because of ...)

items.en: Who usually turns pale?
items.hint: a relative clause: 'quī ...' (he who ...)

items.q: Quandō uxor Iūlium dē epistulā interrogat?
items.en: When does his wife ask Julius about the letter?
items.hint: a 'postquam' clause (after he ...)

items.q: Dē quā rē magister Iūlium in parte posteriōre epistulae monet?
items.en: About what does the master remind Julius in the second part of the letter?
items.hint: ablative after 'dē' (about ...)

items.en: Does this letter contain any praise?
items.hint: a yes/no answer; 'num' expects 'no' (no praise ...)

items.en: What is Marcus's clear answer?
items.hint: nouns with participle and adjective in the nominative

items.en: What is often the clearest answer?
items.hint: a noun in the nominative (the subject)

items.q: Cuius nōmen in parte superiōre tabulae īnscrīptum est?
items.en: Whose name is written at the top of the tablet?
items.hint: a name in the genitive (whose)

items.en: Did Marcus lose Sextus's tablet?
items.hint: a yes/no answer (he did not)

items.en: What is Sextus's tablet like?
items.hint: an adjective in the nominative

items.en: What will Sextus's father think?
items.hint: an accusative with a perfect infinitive (that he ...)

items.en: Why is Marcus now blushing?
items.hint: accusative after 'propter' (because of ...)

items.en: Who usually blushes?
items.hint: a relative clause with 'pudet' (he whom ... shames)

items.q: Quālis puer Mārcus posthāc futūrus est, ut ipse dīcit?
items.en: What kind of boy will Marcus be from now on, as he says?
items.hint: an adjective in the nominative

items.q: Crēditne Iūlius Mārcum prōmissum factūrum esse?
items.en: Does Julius believe Marcus will keep his promise?
items.hint: a yes/no answer (he does not)

items.q: Quotiēs Mārcus hodiē ā magistrō verberātus est?
items.en: How many times was Marcus beaten by the master today?
items.hint: a number adverb (how many times)

items.q: Quem Iūlius iubet Mārcum in cubiculum dūcere?
items.en: Whom does Julius order to take Marcus to his room?
items.hint: a name in the vocative (the person addressed)

items.q: Quid Dāvus posteā Iūliō ferre dēbet?
items.en: What must Davus bring Julius afterwards?
items.hint: a noun in the accusative (the object)

items.q: Cūr haec omnia facta sunt, ut Iūlius dīcit?
items.en: Why did all this happen, according to Julius?
items.hint: a reason clause with 'quod' and a perfect verb

items.en: Who will accompany Marcus tomorrow?
items.hint: a name in the nominative

items.en: Has Marcus been shut in?
items.hint: a yes/no answer (he has)

items.en: What does Aemilia not think?
items.hint: an accusative with a future infinitive (that he will ...)

items.q: Num Iūlius crēdit Mārcum mūtātum esse?
items.en: Does Julius believe that Marcus has changed?
items.hint: a yes/no answer; 'num' expects 'no'

items.q: Quibus rēbus Mārcus melior fierī nōn potest?
items.en: By what means can Marcus not be made better?
items.hint: two nouns in the ablative of means (neither by ... nor by ...)

items.en: To whom is Julius going to write?
items.hint: a noun in the dative (to whom)

items.q: Ā quō epistula Iūliī magistrō trādētur?
items.en: By whom will Julius's letter be handed to the master?
items.hint: a name in the ablative after 'ā' (by whom)

items.q: Cūr magister mercēdem nōn meruit, ut Iūlius dīcit?
items.en: Why hasn't the master earned his fee, according to Julius?
items.hint: a reason: he admits that he can ... (accusative with infinitive)

items.en: What is needed besides being able?
items.hint: an infinitive used as a noun (to want)

items.q: Cūr Iūlius pecūniam solvere nōn potest, ut ipse rīdēns dīcit?
items.en: Why can't Julius pay the money, as he says with a laugh?
items.hint: a reason with a verb of wanting (he does not want to ...)
